# Rules: Desktop app, packaging and updates

**Covers:** `desktop/`, `packaging/`, update channels, the installer, signing.

How to use this file: read the contents list, then read only the entries your change touches (each line gives the line number where the full text starts). The rules that apply to every change are in the root `CLAUDE.md`. To add a rule, see "Adding a rule" there.

## Rules

- **An update stops tidily, and what it interrupted is offered back**
  (v1.249.0, R-02/R-03/R-04/R-06 — the user's Upgrade Ballot). The installer is
  verified BEFORE anything stops: a bad download must never cost a live daemon.
  Then the daemon gets Quit's tidy stop (`requestDaemonShutdown`), and a handoff
  that fails RESPAWNS the children before the dialog — `quitAndInstall` returns
  false and routes failures through its own `error` event, so the teardown must
  not run first. The busy warning counts what the old one could not see: chat
  replies (session_id "chat", no Session row — `core/turns.CHAT_INFLIGHT`) and
  Build panes whose activity is working/blocked, with "Install when idle"
  re-checking every 60 s. `Session.interrupted_at` is the tag the boot reconcile
  writes, ONE `sessions.interrupted` event per boot (never one per session), and
  `GET /sessions/interrupted` feeds one bell row plus one Overview note whose
  Continue clears the tag. CLOSING TO THE TRAY DESTROYS THE RENDERER, so a
  waiting ask is announced by `installAskWatcher` in main.js — never a page
  toast (DesktopNotifyBridge's old comment claimed otherwise); reminders report
  how long the ask has ACTUALLY waited. A shutdown-shaped child exit
  (0x40010004 / session-end) only DEFERS a respawn and is not a crash.
  `classifyStartupFailure` names the cause from the child's exit and its last
  log lines — port in use (uvicorn prints `[Errno 10048]`, not `WinError`), a
  locked database, a failed data upgrade, a missing binary — and the dialog
  offers Retry / Open logs / Quit. R-01 WAS REJECTED BY THE USER:
  `quitAndInstall(false, true)` stays as it is, and nothing relaunches the app
  after a successful install. `tests/test_desktop_reliability_v1249.py`,
  `tests/test_update_busy_v1249.py`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/interrupted-jobs-v1249.test.tsx`.
  v1.400.4 (a USER BUG): twice on 2026-10-27 the FIRST daemon start after an
  update (v1.400.1→.2 and .2→.3) hung inside the lifespan after "Waiting for
  application startup" with nothing more in the log; the 90 s gate showed the
  timeout dialog, the user's Retry relaunched, and the fresh start was ready in
  2 s. 15 earlier updates back to Oct 22 started fine; no Defender event, no
  download mark on the installed files, no orphaned pane shell, so the step is
  NOT known. Two changes: (1) `daemon/boot_watch.BootWatch` (started first
  thing in the lifespan; `_rehydrate_step` and the awaited steps call
  `.step(name)`; `.done()` before the boot summary) logs at 30/60/120 s the
  step and where the boot thread and other busy threads wait, as
  `module:function:line` (module NAMES, never a path or value); it never
  raises into the boot. THE NEXT STUCK START NAMES ITS STEP: read daemon.log
  for "startup has not finished after". (2) desktop/main.js: when the daemon
  gate FAILS and the child is still running (`shouldRetryHungDaemon`: no
  exit code, no signal, not yet retried this launch), the boot restarts ONLY
  the daemon once (`restartDaemonFromShell(why)`, logged "restarting once by
  itself…") and gates again before the dialog; an exited daemon (port taken,
  crash, missing file) goes to the dialog as before.
  `test_startup_speed_v1250::test_neither_gate_is_awaited_a_second_time` now
  allows exactly that one wait inside the retry branch (the serial-wait
  mutation still fails it). Pins: `tests/test_boot_watch_v14004.py` (8
  mutations red).
  v1.400.4 WAS NOT PUBLISHED (Tests and Release each red on a different OLD
  timing test; v1.400.5 ships it): (1) `test_idle_wakeups_v1333::test_an_idle_
  paired_browser_socket_does_not_wake_between_keepalives` read `[1]`: the read
  loop SEEDS itself with one `access_word()` just after `connected` flips, and
  on a loaded runner that seed landed inside the counted second; the test now
  waits for a quiet half second first (`_wait_quiet`, capped, never an
  assertion), and a loop that wakes every 0.25 s still fails it ([1,1,1,1]).
  (2) `test_codex_native_v1365::test_review_a_slow_start_falls_back_for_that_
  call_and_caches_nothing` gave the SECOND call of the target request the
  0.5 s clock too, so a healthy second session that was slow on the runner fell
  back as well; only the first call gets it now. Both reproduced on this PC with
  a plugin that delays the one step (the loop's seed read 0.3 s; the second
  call's request 0.7 s inside its own clock): old shapes CI's exact errors, new
  green.
  v1.407.0 part 6: THE BOOT WATCH CAUGHT IT. The packaged logs (2026-10-26 ..
  10-29, 11 starts after an update) hold FIVE hung starts: 10-27 18:06 and
  18:15 (before the watch: user Quit/Retry), and 10-28 06:52, 10:39, 18:38
  (the watch at 30/60 s, then main.js "restarting once by itself" at 90 s;
  every restart ready in ~2 s). Every caught one: step
  `rehydrate_terminals`, the boot thread in `rehydrate` waiting on the
  restore pool, and EVERY `pane-restore_N` thread in `backend._spawn` ->
  `CreateProcessW` (the user's panes are the WindowsApps `pwsh.EXE` App
  Execution Alias under the bundled ConPTY). Windows never returned the call;
  the event logs show no AppX activation at all in a hung start (a good start
  logs Store license + AppModel container lines at the spawn), and 30 fresh
  processes x 3 parallel first spawns did not reproduce it, so the cause
  inside Windows is NOT known. The fix does not depend on it:
  `terminals/manager.rehydrate` waits at most `RESTORE_WAIT_S` (8 s) — each
  restore on its own DAEMON thread (never a ThreadPoolExecutor: its workers
  are joined at interpreter exit, so a stuck spawn would hang shutdown too);
  a restore finishing inside the bound registers exactly as before (snapshot
  order, one snapshot); a later one registers itself
  (`_finish_late_restore`: slot released, persisted; closed instead when
  `kill_all` began — `_closing`); one still starting keeps its `_reserved`
  slot and its snapshot entry AS READ (`_restoring`, appended by
  `_index_text`, so the 30 s loop, a create or the shutdown snapshot can never
  drop it). `GET /terminals` adds `restoring: [ids]` ONLY when non-empty
  (byte-identical otherwise); the Build page keeps those ids out of
  `prunePaneStorage`/`retainPaneHosts` and re-reads the list every 3 s (≤ 20
  times) to add a late pane. SAME PART, SPEED: the first-spawn PTY verify
  (`_PTY_VERIFY_SECONDS` 0.7) ends as soon as a PUSHING session (raw ConPTY)
  has output — the host prints the moment the shell connects, and a raw
  ConPTY cannot exist without its host (CreatePseudoConsole fails first); a
  POLLED backend keeps the full wait. Measured interleaved on a scratch home
  with two pwsh panes: `rehydrate_terminals` 0.81–1.89 s (median 0.88) ->
  0.12–0.19 s (one cold 1.69), startup total median 3.49 -> 2.85 s;
  spawn-to-healthy was dominated by noisy source-mode imports (6–17 s both).
  DASHBOARD: `DaemonProvider` keeps `checking` true and sets `starting` while
  /health has NEVER answered the page and the page is younger than
  `STARTING_GRACE_MS` (90 s = the desktop gate), re-asking every
  `STARTING_POLL_MS` (1 s); `DaemonBanner` then says `STARTING_TITLE`
  ("Starting Iron Jarvis…", lib/offlineWords) with no warn tone. After a
  first answer a miss is an outage exactly as before. Known: a page's own
  data reads that fail during a start still show their status-0 error until
  the epoch refetch; a pane whose CreateProcessW never returns stays missing
  for that run (it is back next start). Pins:
  `tests/test_boot_pane_restore_bound_v1406.py` (10 mutations red),
  `dashboard/__tests__/{build-restoring,daemon-starting}-v1406.test.tsx`
  (6 mutations red); moved on purpose: `pane-keys-v1280`,
  `terminal-host-v1243` (the kept set is `keep`). REVIEW: a late restore
  registers and THEN persists; a `kill_all` landing between the two killed
  every pane and the late snapshot (no live pane left) wrote an EMPTY index
  over the shutdown snapshot — every pane lost next boot (reproduced). Now
  `_snapshot_lock` serialises every snapshot (taken BEFORE `_lock`), and once
  `_closing` only the inline shutdown snapshot writes (`snapshot` returns,
  `snapshot_if_changed` answers False). Pin:
  `test_a_late_pane_that_opens_just_before_shutdown_cannot_wipe_the_shutdown_snapshot`;
  Build's `retainPaneHosts` keeping a restoring id is pinned too.
  FOLLOW-UPS: (1) while starting, `DaemonBanner` ASKS the desktop shell
  (`watchShell` includes `startingNow`) and `shellKnowsDown` wins over the
  calm line at once: capped, stalled, damaged, or `restarting && restarts > 0`
  — NOT `restarting` alone, which main.js `serviceState` also reports for a
  NORMAL first spawn inside its STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS allowance (`restarts`
  counts unexpected exits only; boot, the tray Restart and the window's
  Restart reset it). (2) every pane still restoring: the Build stage and the
  rail (`PaneRail reopening=`) say "Reopening N terminals…", never the empty
  "No terminals yet" door; a `?focus=` link to a restoring pane keeps that
  target and `activeId` answers null (the stage says "Reopening 1
  terminal…") until it opens or stops restoring. (3) the re-reads go on past
  the first minute every `RESTORING_SLOW_REREAD_MS` (15 s) while `restoring`
  is non-empty, skipped while the window is hidden. Pins: the same two
  dashboard files (11 more mutations red; the empty-door mock now renders its
  title, with a control).

- **Frozen-build verification**: anything touching native deps or subprocess
  spawning MUST be verified in the packaged daemon, not just source. The
  terminals feature shipped dead once because PyInstaller dropped
  `OpenConsole.exe`/`winpty-agent.exe` (now bundled in the .spec). New Python
  deps with native wheels (paramiko/bcrypt/nacl style) need spec entries.

- **Updates come from the `updates` branch manifest first; GitHub's releases
  feed is the FALLBACK, and no raw HttpError ever reaches the Updates page**
  (v1.260.0). electron-updater's GitHub provider opens every check by reading
  `github.com/<repo>/releases.atom`, which GitHub renders in 2–10 s and cuts at
  ~10 s — on 2026-09-14 about every other check on both of the user's PCs 504'd,
  and `friendlyUpdateError` (which knew only the 404 publishing window) printed
  the whole error page plus the `_gh_sess` cookie on the Updates page. Pruning
  331 old releases did NOT change the feed's timing (the count was a wrong
  hypothesis; tags were kept). So: `release.yml` publishes electron-builder's
  `latest.yml` with ABSOLUTE installer URLs (`scripts/publish_update_manifest.py`
  — a line rewrite that refuses a wrong version or a missing sha512) alone on the
  orphan `updates` branch, AFTER `--draft=false`; `desktop/main.js` reads it via
  the generic provider (`UPDATE_MANIFEST_URL`) and `checkForUpdatesWithFallback`
  swaps to `UPDATE_GITHUB_FEED` only when that fails, restoring the manifest for
  the next check. electron-updater EMITS "error" before it rejects, so
  `onUpdaterError` is suppressed while the manifest attempt is armed — the feed
  attempt reports. `updateErrorKind` sorts failures into publishing / transient /
  other; a transient one is one sentence and arms ONE `UPDATE_RETRY_MS` re-check.
  Both workflows trigger on master + tags only, so the `updates` push never
  loops. `tests/test_update_channel_v1260.py` lifts the functions and runs them
  under node; keep owner/repo in `main.js` in step with `desktop/package.json`.

- **A module pops out into its own window, on the other screen when there
  is one** (v1.283.0, pop-out windows). `desktop/main.js` keeps ONE
  BrowserWindow per dashboard route (`popouts` Map; `openPopout` focuses an
  existing one), with the main window's chrome (hidden title bar + native
  overlay, the preload, the token safety net, the external-link guards, a
  per-window `did-fail-load` retry) and NONE of its tray behaviour (no close
  interception; `window-all-closed` stays a no-op; Quit closes them all).
  Placement is `windowState.popoutPlacement(saved, displays, mainBounds,
  offset)` — pure, electron-free, node-tested: the saved rectangle while its
  display exists, else centred on the screen that does NOT hold the main
  window, else cascaded off it; bounds remembered per route in
  `popout-windows.json` (`loadPopoutBounds`/`savePopoutBounds`).
  `normalizePopoutPath` keeps the ironjarvis:// path rules and drops the
  query; "/" never pops out. IPC `popout:open|list|focus|close`, every
  handler `isTrustedDashboardSender`-checked. The renderer learns it is a
  pop-out from the PRELOAD (`--ij-popout=<path>` → `ironjarvis.popout.
  isPopout/path`) — a `?popout=1` would not survive in-window navigation.
  Dashboard: `lib/desktopShell.popoutBridge()/isPopoutWindow()`;
  `lib/nav.labelForPath` (the title bar's rule, now shared); TitleBar's
  `#popout-open` door (desktop, not in a pop-out, never for "/"), the
  `#popout-badge` and the window title via `<html data-ij-title>` (the
  NotificationBell prefixes its count onto that base); Sidebar rows'
  `#popout-row-<route>` hover doors; `DesktopNotifyBridge` stays quiet in a
  pop-out (each window holds its own events socket — one toast per event).
  NOT attached to pop-outs: the renderer watchdog (module-global state; the
  main window keeps it) and `installDashboardReloadOnFailure` (same). Two
  windows on the SAME chat thread both autosave — the thread PUT's
  `updated_at` check is the only guard. Pins:
  `tests/test_desktop_popout_v1283.py`, `dashboard/__tests__/popout-v1283.test.tsx`.

- **A browser tab has no token, and "restart" is not the answer to a 401**
  (v1.264.0). The add-on's Open Jarvis opens the dashboard in the BROWSER; the
  page then 401s everywhere, and the Browser card read its own 401 as "no
  Browser surface — restart Iron Jarvis". Now: `desktop/main.js` owns
  `ironjarvis://` (`setAsDefaultProtocolClient`; packaged AND dev forms), a
  SEPARATE `second-instance` listener registered AFTER the plain one (that one
  is lifted verbatim by `test_desktop_lifecycle_v1192` — the FIRST such block —
  so it must not change shape, and `createMainWindow`'s `loadURL(DASHBOARD_URL)`
  tail is pinned by `test_desktop_reliability_v1226`, so the pending path loads
  AFTER it) plus `open-url` and the cold-start argv all funnel through
  `dashboardPathFromProtocolUrl` (dashboard path only — no host, no dots, no
  `..`, no `//`) into `openDashboardPath`, which shows the window at that page
  or parks it in `pendingProtocolPath` for the first window. The token banner
  outside the desktop shell links `ironjarvis://<path>` (`appLink`, same rule)
  and names `token.txt`; `YourBrowserCard` tells 401/403 ("not signed in")
  from 404 ("older daemon"). Add-on: Enter sends / Steer while running /
  Shift+Enter newline (`keyToPress`, reading the ONE running flag
  `document.body.dataset.turn`); `toggleAction("offline")` is `connect`
  (`resume` resets the backoff and reconnects now); the offline words name the
  cause. `tests/test_sidebar_first_minute_v1264.py`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/sidebar-first-minute-v1264.test.tsx`.

- **The STABLE update channel: a release reaches `updates-stable` only once
  it has been out a day, no newer patch replaced it, its commit's Tests are
  green and it is not held; the daily driver reads it, the other PC stays
  Fresh** (v1.405.0; the user: "55
  releases in 7 days … a Stable update channel for the daily-driver PC").
  WRITER: `.github/workflows/stable.yml` (cron `23 * * * *` + dispatch inputs
  `hold` / `unhold` / `promote`; `permissions: contents: write, actions: read`
  — the read is the Tests verdict, a token's unlisted scopes are none and an
  unread verdict is never green; `concurrency: stable-channel`; inputs reach
  the script through env only) runs `scripts/promote_stable.py` (stdlib, `uv
  run --no-project`), which IMPORTS `publish_update_manifest.rewrite` (never a
  copy) and writes the orphan branch: `latest.yml`, `holds.txt`,
  `promoted.json`, `README.md`. THE RULE is `choose_stable(releases, holds,
  tests_green, now, current, soak_hours=24, promote="")`, pure: the NEWEST
  release that is published (not draft/prerelease), out ≥ 24 h, not held, has
  `latest.yml` + installer + blockmap (state `uploaded`), NOT REPLACED
  (`replaced_by`: a newer published release of the same MAJOR.MINOR — a patch
  is how fixes ship; logged "replaced by vX — waiting for that one"; a newer
  MINOR does not count), whose tag's commit's NEWEST COMPLETED suite run that
  is not `cancelled`/`skipped` concluded `success` (`tests_verdict` over Tests
  runs AND Release runs judged by their `suite` + `python` jobs,
  `release_suite_run`: a skipped suite is no verdict, a green suite with a
  failed publish is green; v1.444.1), and
  newer than what Stable names — never backwards. A newest candidate whose
  verdict was not READ stops the run (`Decision.unread`, exit 5): nothing
  older is promoted, or a Stable PC downloads twice an hour apart. `promote`
  skips the wait and the replacement rule, said in its `why` (refused, exit 3,
  for held / unpublished / Tests not green / not newer). A `latest.yml` that
  fails `stable_manifest` publishes nothing, exit 4. Exits 3–5 still commit
  the hold edits, then the run ends red; 2 (bad input) writes nothing.
  Neither release.yml nor tests.yml triggers on the branch (pinned).
  SHELL: `desktop/main.js` reads `update_channel` at EVERY check
  (`readUpdateChannel`: the state home's config.toml, else
  `~/.ironjarvis/config.toml` — the daemon's own layering; `updateChannelSetting`:
  only a top-level quoted `stable`, forgiving case and spaces like the Config
  validator; anything else is fresh) through ONE `runUpdateCheck(au)` (timer and
  page): Fresh is byte-for-byte the v1.260.0 order (manifest, then the feed);
  Stable reads `UPDATE_STABLE_MANIFEST_URL` ONLY and rethrows (the feed names
  the newest release and would skip the wait) — `onUpdaterError` gives the
  transient words + one retry, `friendlyStableError` says a 404 means Stable
  has nothing to offer yet. A download is judged by the channel the PC is on
  WHEN IT LANDS: `update-available` records where each version was found
  (`_foundOn`, sticky "stable"), `downloadFitsChannel(channel, foundOn)` (Fresh
  takes anything, Stable only what Stable offered; unknown is not), and it is
  applied before every check (`enforceUpdateChannel`: cancels a Fresh download
  in flight via the check result's cancellationToken — electron-updater emits
  `update-cancelled`, not an error — and forgets a waiting one, so a FAILED
  Stable check still drops it), at `update-downloaded` (a Fresh download that
  lands after the switch, or that electron-updater handed a Stable check
  because one was already in progress, is not offered: `forgetPendingUpdate`,
  `autoInstallOnAppQuit = false`, one recheck 15 s later), and before any
  install (`requestUpdateInstall`, `applyPendingUpdate`, the Quit path via
  `dropPendingIfOffChannel`). IPC `update:channels` (sender-checked, both
  manifests' `version:` read at once, 8 s each, null on failure);
  `update:getState` carries `channel`; preload `update.channels`. SETTING:
  schema row `update_channel` (System › Updates, enum fresh/stable,
  `tier="allow", floor_when=("fresh",)` — Fresh widens what reaches the PC),
  Config field (tolerant: not stable = fresh). PAGE:
  `components/settings/UpdateChannelChoice.tsx` + `lib/updateChannel.ts` inside
  the desktop card — the ONE control on Settings › System (`SettingsHome.
  CONTROLLED_IN_SECTION` keeps the plain schema row off the page; a search or
  `?focus=update_channel` opens the Updates section), drawn only when the
  bridge has `channels` (an older shell ignores the setting): saves through
  PUT /settings/values, THEN checks; says when this PC runs a newer version
  than Stable (it stays, no downgrade). HOLD: `core/update_channel.py` +
  `GET/POST /update/stable-hold` (system.py): `gh workflow run stable.yml
  --repo … -f hold=X.Y.Z` through `harness/branches._gh` ONLY with `gh_state`
  signed in, the version X.Y.Z, `confirm: true` (two presses); else the
  command + Actions URL. Its words claim only that the run was ASKED for
  (GitHub keeps one pending run per concurrency group; holds.txt shows a hold
  that landed). THE WAIT IS
  TIME: no word may say a version was tested or ran on the other PC (pinned).
  RELEASE: this commit touches `.github/workflows/*`, so the maintainer pushes
  the TAG by hand (Release flow, step 2). UNVERIFIED: the workflow has never
  run on GitHub (whether `actions: read` is needed was not provable offline;
  a real-data dry run with the user's own gh picked v1.400.7). Pins:
  `tests/test_stable_channel_v14050.py`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/update-channel-v14050.test.tsx`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/settings-update-channel-v14050.test.tsx`; moved on
  purpose: `test_update_channel_v1260` (both call sites go through
  `runUpdateCheck`); the install harnesses of `test_desktop_lifecycle_v1192`,
  `test_desktop_reliability_v1226` and `_v1249` stub `dropPendingIfOffChannel`
  (a PC on Fresh: nothing dropped) — a new harness that lifts an install path
  needs the same stub.

- **The app icon is the user's "iU" tile, at every size Windows draws**
  (v1.380.0; the user pasted the artwork). Pasted pictures are not files:
  it was taken from this conversation's own record (the session `.jsonl`'s
  base64 image block) and kept as `desktop/assets/icon-source.png`.
  `icon.png` = the tile cropped to its rounded square (radius measured on the
  source), corners transparent, 256 RGBA; `icon.ico` = 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48,
  64, 96, 128, 256. `build.win.icon` is the `.ico` (exe, shortcuts, NSIS
  installer/uninstaller); `main.js` `windowIcon()` gives every BrowserWindow
  that sets an icon the `.ico` on Windows (else the `.png`); the tray already
  preferred the `.ico`. The in-app title-bar mark and the dashboard's
  `app/icon.svg` favicon are unchanged (the user asked for the desktop and the
  taskbar). Windows' icon cache can keep the old picture on a shortcut until
  it refreshes. `desktop/assets/README.md` says how to remake the files. Pin:
  `tests/test_app_icon_v1380.py` (red on the old files: 4 of 5).

- **Text size is the window's ZOOM, from one per-device row** (v1.456.0;
  the owner: "change font sizes across the app in settings").
  `device.text_size` (Appearance, allow, store device; options "90"/"100"/
  "110"/"125"/"150", pinned equal to desktop/main.js `TEXT_SIZES` and
  `dashboard/lib/textSize.ts`). It is applied as `webContents.setZoomFactor`
  (desktop/main.js `setTextSize`), never a root font size: most dashboard
  sizes are whole pixels, which rem scaling would not move. Chromium keeps
  zoom per origin (one call reaches every dashboard window) but not across
  restarts, so main keeps `textSize` in desktop-settings.json and
  `installTextSizeHooks` re-applies it on every dashboard page's
  `did-finish-load` (the loading splash is never zoomed). The View menu's
  Ctrl + = / - / 0 and Ctrl + wheel (`zoom-changed`) call `stepTextSize`
  (ends clamp, 0 = normal), which applies it and sends `textSize:changed` to
  that window; `DeviceSettingsBridge` saves it as the row
  (`lib/deviceSettings.chooseTextSize`). A row set from Settings or chat
  reaches the shell through `applyOne` → `lib/textSize.applyTextSize` →
  preload `textSize.set` (IPC sender-checked). NEVER put Chromium's
  `resetZoom`/`zoomIn`/`zoomOut` roles back in the menu: they zoom without
  telling the setting. A browser tab has no bridge: the row is saved, the
  help says to use the browser's zoom. Trigger aliases cover "text size",
  "font size", "bigger/larger/smaller text"; a font size "in my report" arms
  no writer (`_about_something_else`). Pins: `tests/test_text_size_v14560.py`,
  `dashboard/__tests__/text-size-v1456.test.tsx`.

- **The installer is SIGNED when six secrets are set; a signed build is
  checked by Windows before it is kept** (v1.470.1; Microsoft Artifact
  Signing, publisher `RealDealCPA.Ai LLC`, account `ironjarvissign`, profile
  `ironjarvis-public`; `docs/SIGNING.md`). `desktop/build-installer.ps1`:
  all of AZURE_TENANT_ID / AZURE_CLIENT_ID / AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET /
  IJ_SIGN_ENDPOINT / IJ_SIGN_ACCOUNT / IJ_SIGN_PROFILE present → `--config
  builder-signed.js` (package.json's own build block + `win.azureSignOptions`;
  electron-builder 26 then installs the TrustedSigning PowerShell module and
  signs every .exe and the installer); none → unsigned as before; some → the
  build stops. NEVER put `azureSignOptions` or a `win.sign` key in
  package.json itself (a bare `win.sign` once failed config validation and
  shipped an empty release; and package.json alone must stay a working
  unsigned build). release.yml's `Check the installer's signature` step
  (`id: signature`, output `signed`) requires a Valid Authenticode signature
  by the publisher with a timestamp on the installer, `Iron Jarvis.exe` and
  the daemon, boots the SIGNED daemon, and feeds `INSTALLER_SIGNED` to the
  publish job, which picks `RELEASE_NOTES_SIGNED`. Repo variable
  `IJ_REQUIRE_SIGNED=true` (set it after the first signed release) fails an
  unsigned build: a signed install refuses an unsigned update, because
  electron-builder writes the publisher into app-update.yml. The owner types
  the secrets into GitHub; never take the client secret through chat.
  v1.470.1 was the FIRST SIGNED RELEASE (2026-11-10; the published installer
  read Valid, signer RealDealCPA.Ai LLC, issuer Microsoft ID Verified CS,
  timestamped) and `IJ_REQUIRE_SIGNED` is now `true`: EVERY release from here
  must sign, so a lapsed Azure subscription or an expired client secret fails
  the release at the installer job. v1.470.2: README and the Help page say
  the installer is signed. Pins: `tests/test_installer_signing_v14701.py`.
  Try a workflow change with `gh workflow run release.yml --ref <branch> -f
  dry_run=true` (it signs for real, publishes nothing).

- `desktop/main.js` — supervisor (auto-restart children), tray, global
  hotkeys (Ctrl+Shift+J window, Ctrl+Shift+Space Spotlight), updater +
  update IPC, native clipboard IPC, media permissions. `preload.js` exposes
  `window.ironjarvis` (token, clipboard, update bridge).

- **The desktop adds the token only to a request the DASHBOARD made, kills only its own daemons, and never logs the token** (v1.499.3 review). `shouldInjectAuth` (pure): our daemon port, no Authorization of its own, and a dashboard Origin (or, with none, a dashboard referrer/frame); a dev page previewed in Chat › Code's Browser pane used to get full daemon access. The orphan sweep lists `ironjarvis.exe` (bounded PowerShell CIM) and kills by PID only those under the app's own daemon folder (a dev `.venv` daemon was killed); it falls back to its own child. `redactSecrets` masks `token=`, `Bearer` and the live token in renderer.log and the desktop log. OPEN: verify on the packaged build (Origin visibility in webRequest, the sweep on update/Quit); `installer.nsh` still kills by image name. Pins: `tests/test_desktop_trust_fixes_v1499.py`.

- **The updater has ONE name for the system it serves (`UPDATE_PLATFORM`),
  Linux reads its OWN branches, and every Linux path sits behind that name**
  (v1.517.0). `updateBaseFor(url)` turns `…/updates` into `…/updates-linux`
  (and `-stable` into `-stable-linux`) on Linux only;
  `updateManifestFileFor()` is `latest-linux.yml` there; `_setUpdateSource`
  and `readChannelVersions` go through both. `updateErrorKind` reads a
  missing `latest(-linux)?.yml` as "publishing" (every Linux preview showed
  the raw "Cannot find latest-linux.yml" on each check). `initUpdater`
  returns null on Linux when `linuxCanSelfUpdate()` is false (no `APPIMAGE`
  and no `resources/package-type`): the page says "unsupported" instead of a
  check that never ends (`AppImageUpdater.isUpdaterActive()` is false and
  `checkForUpdates` then resolves with no event). `cachedInstallerState`
  looks under `XDG_CACHE_HOME`/`~/.cache` on Linux. Two things
  electron-updater's AppImage path needs from the app: the NEW file is
  started with `APPIMAGE_EXIT_AFTER_INSTALL=true` when an update installs on
  Quit and must leave at once (the guard is the first code after the
  requires), and after `quitAndInstall(false, true)` it is started while the
  old app still holds the single-instance lock (`lockAfterUpdate`, only when
  `APPIMAGE_SILENT_INSTALL` is set). `updateRehearsalUrl()` accepts exactly
  `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` from `IRONJARVIS_UPDATE_REHEARSAL_URL`, on Linux
  only; with `IRONJARVIS_UPDATE_REHEARSAL_INSTALL=restart` the app applies
  the download itself. THE PINS RUN BOTH SYSTEMS ON ANY MACHINE: the older
  harnesses (`test_update_channel_v1260`, `test_stable_channel_v14050`,
  `test_desktop_reliability_v1249`) declare `UPDATE_PLATFORM = "win32"`,
  `tests/test_linux_self_update_v1517.py` runs both. A new updater function
  that differs by system reads `UPDATE_PLATFORM`, never `process.platform`,
  or its pin tests one system on Windows and another on Linux.

- **On Linux the shell's "start at login" is an autostart ENTRY, the tray
  icon is the png, and a restart starts the FILE the user runs** (v1.519.0).
  Electron's `setLoginItemSettings`/`getLoginItemSettings` do nothing on
  Linux (the switch read On and nothing started): `setStartAtLogin` writes
  `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/autostart/iron-jarvis.desktop` (`linuxAutostartEntry`:
  `Exec="<APPIMAGE or execPath>" --hidden`, the path quoted by the
  desktop-entry rules) and removes it for Off; `getStartAtLogin` is "the
  file exists"; `refreshLinuxAutostart()` at start rewrites an entry that is
  ON when the single file was moved. `startAtLoginWorksHere()` (packaged, on
  win32 or linux) replaces the four `process.platform === "win32"` gates in
  the desktop-switches section; the first-run QUESTION stays Windows-only
  (its words name Windows). `createTray` takes `icon.ico` only when
  `process.platform !== "linux"` (nativeImage cannot read an .ico there).
  Inside an AppImage `process.execPath` is in a mount that is gone once the
  app closes, so `app.relaunch` is wrapped ONCE, right after the requires,
  to pass `execPath: process.env.APPIMAGE`; every call site still reads
  `app.relaunch();` (pinned by `test_desktop_reliability_v1249`). Pins:
  `tests/test_linux_desktop_v1519.py` (its node harness sets
  `process.platform`, so the Linux and the Windows path both run on any
  machine). NOT VERIFIED on a Linux desktop: the restart wrap (no test can
  open the Retry dialog), the tray picture itself.

- **The connected apps' bridge is its own signed one-file program, shipped in `resources/bridge` with `bridge-id.txt`; a build without it fails** (v1.538.0, fourth review MS2/MS3).
  `packaging/ironjarvis.spec` builds `ironjarvis-bridge` from `src/iron_jarvis/mcpserver/stdio_shim.py` itself (excludes `iron_jarvis` and `ssl`; the build fails on a leaked module or over 25 MB) into `packaging/dist/bridge/`; `build_daemon.ps1` and `afterPack.js` refuse a build without it; `release.yml` runs its `--check` after the freeze and again on the signed copy, whose signature is checked with the others. The daemon's start step `refresh_bridge` (off the loop, bounded) copies it and moves older entries; backups skip `<home>/bridge/`; the Doctor row is "The connected apps' bridge". Never name the bridge `ironjarvis.exe`: the installer and the sweep kill that name. Pins: `tests/test_fourth_review_bridge_packaging_v1538.py`.

- **A Linux start-at-sign-in entry is written only for a path that GLib and systemd both start; anything else is refused in words, and no false On is left** (v1.540.0, fourth review LX4, LX5, C-LX-2).
  Measured on ubuntu-latest (GLib 2.88, systemd 259): systemd's service manager refuses `"`, `'` and `\` in a program path (its autostart generator also turns `$` and `` ` `` into `\$` and `` \` ``, which the manager then refuses), and GLib and the generator both look for the program before they turn `%%` into `%`; no desktop-entry spelling of such a path starts under both. `desktopEntryExecArg` refuses those characters and control characters (null) and otherwise only double-quotes; `setStartAtLogin` writes nothing and removes an old entry, `refreshLinuxAutostart` removes an entry it cannot write, and the menu records Off and says `LINUX_AUTOSTART_REFUSED_HOW`. Recovery sentences go through `releasesHow(<constant>)`: Windows' words unchanged; Linux names `Iron-Jarvis-amd64.deb` or `Iron-Jarvis-x86_64.AppImage` (`linuxInstallKind`) and opens the releases list. A harness that lifts a caller lifts `releasesHow` and declares `UPDATE_PLATFORM`. A Linux `_updateState` carries `install`, and the Updates card shows one line for it; Windows sends none. Pins: `tests/test_fourth_review_linux_desktop_v1540.py`, `dashboard/__tests__/fourth-review-linux-updates-v1540.test.tsx`, and the real-parser proof `tests/test_fourth_review_linux_autostart_real_v1540.py` (desktop-file-validate, GLib, the generator and a real `systemctl --user` start, on the Linux gate; samples from `scripts/linux_autostart_samples.mjs`).

- **Quick Ask's answer appears in ONE small window where the box was, never in the main window; only that window's own dashboard frame takes the words, hides it or moves its chat** (v1.563.0, next leaps 36-a, R2.2, D-36.1).
  `runSpotlightTask` keeps the words in `pendingQuickAsk` as before and calls `openQuickAnswer`, which hides the box and builds (or reuses, ONE at a time) `quickAnswerWin` at `quickAnswerBounds(box, workArea)` (480 by 560, centred under the box, clamped) on `quickAnswerUrl` (`/chat?new=1&quick=1&compact=1&popout=1`; never the words). It is built like a pop-out (main `preload.js`, the token argument and safety net, `--ij-popout=/chat`, `setWindowOpenHandler`, `will-redirect`, `did-fail-load` retry of the same address, `installPopoutCrashReload`) plus `--ij-quick-answer=1`, `alwaysOnTop` "floating" (the box keeps "screen-saver"), `skipTaskbar`, not minimisable; it is NOT in `popouts`, so it never speaks for the app and its bell stays quiet. No blur handler (D-36.1); `close` hides it unless `isQuitting`/`shuttingDown`; hidden for `SPOTLIGHT_IDLE_DESTROY_MS` it is destroyed by its OWN timer (`scheduleQuickAnswerDestroy`; sharing the box's would cancel one with the other). `toggleSpotlight` first calls `focusQuickAnswer` (on screen: focus + `quick-ask:focus` to the page). Another dashboard page is the main window's: `will-navigate` and `did-navigate-in-page` send it through `quickAnswerMainPath` to `openDashboardPath` and step the small window back. IPC: `quick-ask:take` (`quickAskTake`), `quick-ask:to-main` (`quickAskToMain`: `{thread}` matching `QUICK_THREAD_RX` opens `/chat?thread=` there and hides the small window, `{path}` a door), `quick-ask:hide` (`quickAskHide`), each `isTrustedDashboardSender` AND `isFromQuickAnswer` (the sender IS the answer window's webContents). Dashboard: `lib/quickAnswer` (`isCompactChat`: in the desktop app the preload's `quickAsk.isAnswerWindow` ALONE, so a `?compact=1` in the main window draws the full page; `?compact=1` only in a browser; `CompactChatContext`, provided by `ChatCodeSurface` from its layout effect with the chat kept at the same tree position so it never remounts; `useAnswerWindow`: Esc hides unless defaultPrevented or a `[aria-modal]`/menu/listbox is open, a link to another page goes to `toMainWindow({path})`, `mainWindowPath` keeps `/chat?thread=` here). Esc in the answer window NEVER answers an approval or an app's question (review): `DockAsk` reads `CompactChatContext`, its `press("decline")` refuses, and from inside an app's card (which stops its keys) it calls `hideAnswerWindow` itself; the keys line is `dockAskKeyHint(kind, item, {escAnswers: escAnswersCard(item, compact)})` (Enter only). Those wait in the chat and the bell (daemon turns). The Local only question (`cloud`) is the exception (`lib/dockAsk.escAnswersCard`, second review): it is page state asked before anything is sent or saved, so hiding over it lost the words; Esc there is still "Keep it local" (sends and records nothing, the words back in the box) and the window stays in that press, because the card carries `data-esc-answers`, which `escapeHidesWindow` treats as in front. In compact `ChatCodeSurface` never calls `choose("code")`: `CHAT_VIEW_EVENT` code, `BUILD_SESSION_EVENT` and `BUILD_NIGHT_EVENT` go to `toMainWindow` (`CODE_VIEW_HREF`, `buildSessionHref`, `lastNightHref`), and `view === "code" && !compact` covers a remembered view; `components/chat/QuickAskHeader` ("Continue in the main window", disabled until the chat is saved), and the chat page's compact branches (no rail, no top bar, no drawer, no hero, `!max-h-none`, `escStops={false}` so Esc mid-reply hides and does not stop). The turn body is the ordinary stream lane's (pinned equal), so `tests/test_profile_v1144.py` gains no compact case: the daemon never hears of compact. The layout at 480 by 560 and 390 px is measured in a real browser by `dashboard/e2e/quick-ask-window.spec.ts` (local only, like every e2e spec): in compact the row under the composer (`composer-meta`) drops the map and takes no room when empty (`empty:hidden`); `DemoConnectChoice` stays there because the demo note (`DEMO_NOTE_FIX_CHAT`) points at "the button just below the message box", so with the demo strip and that offer up the messages get the least room (the spec's `room.demo`), and once a real model answers they get `room.everyday`. A hand-over goes WITH its page (third review): a door that stages the user's request in sessionStorage (the coding door, the team door, a workflow draft's Open in editor) staged it in the answer window's storage, which the main window cannot read, so its page opened empty; the capture-phase link catch now leaves a host-handled door (`OWN_PRESS_ATTR`, set by `DoorsStrip` when `onOpen` is given) to the page's `openDoor`, whose compact branch stages and calls `doorToMainWindow`, and `toMainWindow({path})` sends what this window staged for that page (`MAIN_WINDOW_HAND_OVERS`, twin of main.js `QUICK_CARRY_KEYS`, pinned equal) as `carry`; `quickAskToMain` holds it in `pendingMainCarry` (`quickCarryFor`: that page's own key only, at most `QUICK_CARRY_MAX_CHARS`), and the main window's preload takes it SYNCHRONOUSLY before the page runs (`quick-ask:carry`, `quickAskCarry`: `isFromMainWindow`, the exact path, `QUICK_ASK_TTL_MS`, once) into that window's sessionStorage, so the Code view keeps the words and Local only. A file pressed in the record continues the chat in the main window with that file open (`{thread, file}` → `QUICK_CARRY_FILE_KEY`, read by `takeMainWindowFile` after `openThread`); `OPEN_PLACE_EVENT` is left unanswered in compact, so a figure says its place in words. Closing the window over the Local only question discards it (said in the Handbook). OPEN: not opened in the packaged app (window placement, the overlay's buttons, keyboard focus when the window shows after its page drew, `did-navigate-in-page` + `navigationHistory.goBack` on Electron 42). Pins: `tests/test_leap36a_answer_window.py`, `tests/test_north_star_quick_window_v1506.py` (moved on purpose), `dashboard/__tests__/leap-36a-compact-chat.test.tsx`, `dashboard/__tests__/leap-36a-hand-over.test.tsx`.
